title: Absorption And First-Pass Flow
description: Dose form -> dissolution -> membrane crossing -> portal blood -> gut wall/liver metabolism -> systemic circulation.
interaction: Click each step to reveal the factor that can slow or reduce exposure.

title: Insulin Receptor Signaling
description: Insulin receptor tyrosine kinase activation leading to PI3K/Akt, GLUT4 translocation, glycogen synthesis, and potassium shift into cells.
interaction: Reveal metabolic effects by tissue: liver, muscle, adipose.

title: IV Anaesthetic Comparison
description: Propofol, thiopental, etomidate, and ketamine compared by mechanism, hemodynamic effect, analgesia, and major cautions.
interaction: Filter by clinical situation such as unstable patient, bronchospasm, or outpatient procedure.

title: Enteral Route Comparison
description: Oral, sublingual, buccal, and rectal routes compared by first-pass effect, onset, and reliability.
interaction: Select a route to show its exam advantages and limitations.

title: Adrenergic Receptor Effect Table
description: Adrenaline, noradrenaline, dopamine, and isoprenaline mapped to alpha and beta receptor effects.
interaction: Highlight receptor effects relevant to anaphylaxis and shock.

title: Dependence Reward Pathway
description: VTA -> nucleus accumbens -> prefrontal cortex reward pathway with tolerance, dependence, addiction, and withdrawal terms.
interaction: Toggle terms to compare dependence, tolerance, and addiction.

title: Volume Of Distribution Model
description: Low and high Vd examples showing plasma binding, tissue binding, barriers, and loading dose logic.
interaction: Change protein binding or tissue binding to see how apparent Vd changes.

title: G-Protein Coupled Receptor Pathways
description: Gs, Gi, and Gq signaling with receptor examples and second messengers.
interaction: Click each G-protein to reveal receptor examples and clinical drug links.

title: Dose-Response Curves
description: Potency, efficacy, competitive antagonism, and noncompetitive antagonism on dose-response curves.
interaction: Overlay agonist, partial agonist, and antagonist curves.

title: Therapeutic Index Graph
description: ED50, TD50, LD50, therapeutic index, and therapeutic window.
interaction: Compare a wide-window drug with a narrow-window drug.

title: Renal Drug Excretion
description: Glomerular filtration, tubular secretion, and tubular reabsorption with urine pH effects.
interaction: Toggle weak acid or weak base to predict ion trapping.

title: Phase I And Phase II Metabolism
description: CYP-mediated oxidation/reduction/hydrolysis and conjugation reactions with induction and inhibition notes.
interaction: Match common inducers and inhibitors to expected drug level changes.

title: Drug Interaction Types
description: Pharmaceutical, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic interactions with high-risk examples.
interaction: Classify examples by interaction type.

title: Cephalosporin Generation Ladder
description: Cephalosporin generations with Gram-negative expansion, Pseudomonas, MRSA, and key exam examples.
interaction: Select a generation to reveal coverage and high-yield uses.

title: Pharmacovigilance Signal Flow
description: Adverse event report -> signal detection -> assessment -> risk minimization -> regulatory action.
interaction: Open terms: ADR, AE, signal, PSUR, risk management plan.

title: Dose Types Map
description: Single, daily, therapeutic, toxic, loading, maintenance, and cumulative dose relationships.
interaction: Connect dose type to the pharmacokinetic parameter that determines it.

title: Drug Allergy Types
description: Gell-Coombs type I-IV drug allergy mechanisms and clinical examples.
interaction: Match clinical reactions to immune mechanism.

title: Pregnancy Toxicity Timeline
description: Preimplantation, organogenesis, fetal period, and peripartum toxicity risks.
interaction: Place example drugs on the pregnancy risk timeline.

title: ADR ABCDEF Classification
description: Type A augmented, B bizarre, C chronic, D delayed, E end-of-use, and F failure reactions.
interaction: Classify an adverse reaction by predictability and dose relation.

title: Penicillin Subclass Map
description: Natural, depot, penicillinase-resistant, aminopenicillin, and antipseudomonal penicillin groups.
interaction: Reveal spectrum and classic exam traps by subclass.

title: Bioavailability Curve
description: AUC, Cmax, Tmax, and first-pass metabolism on plasma concentration-time curves.
interaction: Compare oral and IV curves.

title: Prescription Structure
description: Patient data, prescriber data, Rp., subscription, signatura, date, and authentication.
interaction: Click a prescription field to see what belongs there.
